text_summary.body: John mentions the Feast of the Dedication at Jerusalem in winter, the festival commemorating this rededication.

setting.period: Seleucid rule over Judaea; reign of Antiochus IV (175–164 BC)
setting.body: Antiochus IV's measures culminated in the "abomination of desolation" on the altar on 15 Chislev 145 SE (1 Macc 1:54). Three years later, on 25 Chislev 148, Judas Maccabaeus's party dedicated a new altar and instituted an eight-day festival (1 Macc 4:52–59), which Josephus says was called "Lights". The Babylonian King List reports Antiochus's death in Kislîmu 148 (Babylonian reckoning).

rulers.role: Seleucid king who suppressed Temple worship
